rows.note: This is the all-purpose choice for moving around without a clear purpose or destination.

example.english: They often wander around, asking wherever they see a help-wanted sign.
example.traditional: 佢哋成日周圍咁行，見到邊度請人就入去問下。
example.jyutping: keoi5 dei6 seng4 jat6 zau1 wai4 gam3 haang4 gin3 dou2 bin1 dou6 cing2 jan4 zau6 jap6 heoi3 man6 haa5

rows.note: Use this when a person, route, or line of thought veers away from its intended course.

example.english: This route has begun to wander off course, so let’s turn back.
example.traditional: 呢條路行偏咗，返轉頭啦。
example.jyutping: ni1 tiu4 lou6 haang4 pin1 zo2 faan1 zyun3 tau4 laa1

rows.note: Use this specifically when a writer or speaker wanders away from the subject under discussion.

example.english: You always wander off topic; let’s get back to the report first.
example.traditional: 你講講下又離題喇，返返去份報告先啦。
example.jyutping: nei5 gong2 gong2 haa5 jau6 lei4 tai4 laa3 faan1 faan1 heoi3 fan6 bou3 gou3 sin1 laa1

rows.note: Use this when someone mentally drifts or is absent-minded rather than physically wandering.

example.english: You seem to wander in your thoughts today—didn’t you get enough sleep?
example.traditional: 你今日成個人游魂咁，係咪冇瞓夠呀？
example.jyutping: nei5 gam1 jat6 seng4 go3 jan4 jau4 wan4 gam3 hai6 mai6 mou5 fan3 gau3 aa3
